source.title: Mask2Shield: Strengthening LLM Safety against Neuron-Pruning Attacks
source.authors: Jin-Cheng Ying; Ming-Hui Xu; Yin-Hao Xiao; Xiu-Zhen Cheng; Wen-Cheng Yang

record.tranche_reason: The paper cites the single-residual-direction finding and explicitly distinguishes it from its own experiments, which target selector-identified FFN channels. It reports no residual-direction intervention or measurement, so it neither tests nor uses the claim itself.
record.gate_note: The paper states that its experiments test FFN-channel pruning, not arbitrary residual-stream direction interventions. The rows record its own related findings on channel pruning and refusal; none directly tests a claim version. Cited results from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper studies FFN-channel (neuron) pruning attacks and a masked-forward training defense. It cites Arditi et al. only in related work, saying direction ablation can disable refusal without editing FFN channels. It states that it tests selector-identified channel pruning, 'rather than robustness to arbitrary residual-stream direction interventions'. No difference-in-means direction is computed, ablated, added or weight-edited. All results concern a related but different construct: FFN-channel safety neurons.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that M2S reduces the success of recomputed neuron-pruning attacks across ten configurations and transfers to TwinBreak. They also conclude that aggressive pruning damages coherent generation before restoring harmful compliance. They note that capability cost is architecture-dependent, largest for Gemma.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains against selector-identified FFN-channel masks and evaluates channel-pruning attacks; it does not implement the original residual-stream difference-in-means direction method.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by model and attack pipeline. The paper reports architecture-dependent capability trade-offs, and validity falls sharply above 2% cumulative targeted pruning in its budget sweep.

fits_no_version.finding: Under recomputed FULL(SN−) FFN-channel pruning, Base checkpoints give 80–279/313 successful attacks and M2S checkpoints give 1–44/313 (Table I). M2S is above the cited SafeNeuron rows for Qwen2.5-7B (35 vs 183 is lower; Gemma 30 vs 23 is higher). M2S is lower than Base in every configuration.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Masked-forward training against FFN-channel masks reduces the success of recomputed neuron-pruning attacks on refusal.

fits_no_version.finding: Under TwinBreak iteration 5, M2S checkpoints stay at 0–15% ASR versus published baselines of about 89–99%. The residual attack success depends on model and evaluation set.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The masked-forward defense transfers to a different neuron-selection and pruning pipeline.

fits_no_version.finding: Cumulative targeted deletion on defended LLaMA-3.2-1B gives 1–18/313 attacks up to 5% removal. Output validity falls from 313/313 at 2% to 213/313 at 5% and 0/313 at 10%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: After this defense, refusal is not concentrated in a small removable FFN-channel set.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing the training mask or using a same-size random mask leaves the attack effective (103–225/313). Removing the benign KL term keeps attack counts low but raises GSM8K refusal-keyword matches to 27–73/100.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Both the selected mask and the teacher-preservation term are needed for the reported outcome.

record.problems: The study tests FFN-channel pruning rather than the claimed residual-stream direction. Some capability costs are architecture-dependent, and the cumulative-pruning validity measure comes from a separate model judge. Table IV's refusal-rate diagnostic is lexical rather than semantic. The paper reports uncertainty for benchmark accuracies, but not for the attack-count results.
record.rows_left_out: The four capability benchmark scores in Table I are not listed individually because they do not test any claim version or the related channel-pruning refusal outcome directly. Table II iterations 1–4 and TP-100 columns are omitted; the table's fifth-iteration validation results were retained for each model and evaluation metric. Table IV's No KL and M2S keyword-count rows were retained because the paper explicitly contrasts these response-pattern measures; other variant keyword counts were omitted.

untested.parts: No residual-stream difference-in-means direction; no ablation or addition.
No jailbreak analysed for direction suppression; no training against direction ablation (DeepRefusal only cited).
Harm judgment and refusal not separated.
Training effect tested only for FFN-channel concentration, not for the direction.
DeepSeek-R1-Distill is included only in channel-pruning tests.

record.verdict_notes: The record's first fits_no_version entry wrongly compared M2S with SafeNeuron rows as if they were Base; it is corrected here. Table II rows alternate Val/TP-100 values with iteration-5 Val last, which caused several misreadings. None of the rows bears on any version of the residual-direction claim.

versions.untested_parts: No difference-in-means residual direction is found, added, or ablated; no direction-specific refusal or capability outcome is measured.
No weight edit implementing ablation of the claimed residual-stream direction is tested.
No attack is tested for suppressing the claimed residual-stream direction, and no training against that direction's ablation is evaluated.
The study does not compare residual-stream direction geometries such as a single direction, affine structure, or cone.
The study does not separate harmfulness judgment from refusal decision representations.
No transfer of the claimed residual-stream direction across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct stages is tested.
The study trains against FFN-channel masking but does not test whether refusal-training history determines whether the claimed direction exists.
A DeepSeek reasoning-model configuration is included in channel-pruning experiments, but the claimed direction is not tested in reasoning models.
